chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Muhammad, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked him about a person in ihram who was compelled to eat game or meat of an animal that died naturally. He said: 'Which do you prefer to eat, the game or the meat of an animal that died naturally?' I said: 'The meat of an animal that died naturally, because the game is forbidden to the person in ihram.' He said: 'Which do you prefer to eat, from your own wealth or the meat of an animal that died naturally?' I said: 'I eat from my own wealth.' He said: 'Then eat the game and ransom it.'

key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: Person in ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.وَالْمَيْتَةِ: And the meat of an animal that died naturally (carrion)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim in ihram who is forced to eat game?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in the context of *kaffarah* (expiation) for unintentional violations of ihram restrictions, highlighting the principle of *darurah* (necessity) overriding prohibition. The Imam employs a comparative analogy (*qiyas*) to establish that while the game is forbidden, consuming it under duress is permissible provided the pilgrim compensates with their own wealth, thereby preserving the sanctity of the pilgrimage rites while addressing physical need.
